thread.title_full: Camden's $38M fiscal budget lowers tax rate by 2 cents - NewsBreak

author: Savannah Hess
title: Camden's $38M fiscal budget lowers tax rate by 2 cents - NewsBreak
text:
By Savannah Hess ,
1 hours ago Camden County residents should find some relief with their next property tax statement after the Board of Commissioners voted to reduce the rate from 74 cents to 72 cents per $100 valuation, Tuesday, June 23.
The decision came as part of commissioners’ adoption of the county’s $38.87 million 2026–27 fiscal budget. The decrease in tax rate is the first since at least 2024 when it was still 74 cents.
The budget totals just under $39 million, of which roughly 26.84 million makes up the county’s general fund, The general fund is used to finance county operations and services.
Education accounts for about 23% of departmental spending, with $5.63 million for school operations, $400,000 for capital needs, and continued funding of 20.5% of the school system’s overall budget.
Public safety upgrades include new reporting software, Axon contracts, a detective pay adjustment, and two patrol vehicles for the Sheriff’s Office, plus a new EMS supervisor vehicle and $40,000 for design work and engineering for a combined parks and recreation/senior center.
Community services will expand through opioid settlement funding that converts a part‑time FOCUS 4-H role to a full-time position. The county also budgeted for furnishing the all new Treasure Point Extension Office, shifting the librarian salary to county payroll, and maintaining regional partnerships, including $167,895 for Pasquotank Animal Shelter services. The budget became effective July 1.
There will be an increase in the solid waste fee from $50 to $150 as well as the base water rate from $1.50 to $30.
“We’ve raised fees this year to put more of an onus on incoming development, so we should see an increase in revenue from those streams,” said Dr. Jason Banks, the commission chairman. “On the flip side, it would be nice to provide relief to our current, longstanding citizens,”
The budget also invests in major water and wastewater projects, including engineering and design work for a new South Mills treatment plant, construction of a clear well at the reverse osmosis facility this fall, and a three-year radio-read meter replacement program.
